rationale.B: Candy Grapple improves removal, Back for Seconds improves recursion, and Beseech the Mirror improves a search spell. These independent applications make Bargain a core black mechanic in the set, supporting Primary.
rationale.R: Torch the Tower and Stonesplitter Bolt upgrade damage, while Realm-Scorcher Hellkite rewards Bargain with mana. Red uses the mechanic on both spells and a major creature threat, supporting Primary rather than a restricted exception.
rationale.G: Brave the Wilds adds land animation, Troublemaker Ouphe removes an artifact or enchantment, and Hamlet Glutton becomes cheaper. These varied uses show a core green implementation, supporting Primary.

limitations: The evidence is chiefly one set's deliberate implementation, not proof of frequent use throughout Magic.

access_review.scope: The Blight action puts -1/-1 counters on a creature controlled by the player who blights.
access_review.summary: The reviewed white, blue, black and red cards use Blight. Green appears in multicolor examples, which are listed as combinations.

W.note: The reviewed white cards use Blight to exile an enchanted creature, return an Aura from the graveyard, or choose both modes of a spell. These examples establish white access.

U.note: Wild Unraveling counters a spell and requires either blight 2 or an extra {1} as an additional casting cost. This supplies a blue example.

B.note: Blighted Blackthorn uses Blight for cards, Dawnhand Dissident uses it in activated abilities, and Bogslither's Embrace uses it in removal.

R.note: Gristle Glutton uses Blight in an ability that discards a card, then draws a card. Scuzzback Scrounger uses it to make Treasure, and Cinder Strike uses it to strengthen removal.

G.note: The reviewed green examples are multicolor cards: Auntie Ool, Cursewretch, High Perfect Morcant. They are listed under combinations; no single-color green example was found in this scope.

combinations.note: Auntie Ool, Cursewretch provides a black-red-green example. This card documents this combination, not separate single-color sources.
Chaos Spewer, Shadow Urchin provide black-red examples. These cards document this combination, not separate single-color sources.
High Perfect Morcant provides a black-green example. This card documents this combination, not separate single-color sources.

colorless.note: No colorless example was found in the reviewed scope.

limitations: Access describes the colors of the reviewed cards or mechanic-bearing faces, not Commander deck legality. Multicolor cards and colorless grants do not establish separate single-color sources.
